questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose Maastricht over other universities because of its courses. As the Treaty of Maastricht was signed here, the university has a lot of competance on EU-law.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Generally I was very happy with the city and its people. However, I found the studies load to be a bit too intensive. This made social life more dificult, since all the law students spent quite a lot of time on preparing for the courses.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. UM has an informative website. And the Exchange Officer is very helpfull if you send a e-mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Informative e-mails and some days of introduction.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at a UM guesthouse. It was very easy to get, if you book early (around april). This is an advantage as the housing situation i Maastricht can be quite difficult.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
UM guesthouse is just like a normal dorm room with shared kitchen. It works fine.

The downside is, that it's a bit expensive for just a dorm room. You can look for something cheaper and better if you have time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a pretty simple online platform for course registration.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just register at their online platform using the guidance that they send by e-mail.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They send guidance by e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I got all the classes, I wanted. 

During the semester, I changed my mind and switched one class with another. This went quite smooth with the help of the Exchange Officer.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The proces was easy in my experiance, so I don't really have any advice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The courses are very interesting and the professors are very capable.

Half of the education are lectures and the other half are tutorials. In the lectures you just listen to the professor and take notes. In the tutorials the professer let the students take the lead under the PBL-style (problem based learning).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
In the tutorials the students are expected to learn from discussing with each other in class. In some courses a discussion leader is appointed among the students. In order to be ready for this, a lot of studying is needed before the tutorials. However, it varies from course to course how much information the professor gives. 

The learning material is mostely judgements, articles and so on. We didn't use the textbooks that much, which was also more challenging. 

But it should be said that the vast majority of students passes the exam in the first try.

Most of the exams are 2 hours written. Sometimes with aditional papers to submit. 

Maybe, the study load will be lighter if you choose different courses than me.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The lectures are pretty much the same.

The tutorials at UM are similar to those at UCPH. But at UM you have to learn more with your follow students, and the professor don't have slides and don't always give a clear answer.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Evidence (MA, not that hard, but taught in a confusing way)
Advanced european Law (MA, less hard and taought in a structured way)
Global environmental law (MA, less hard and taught in a structured way)
European fundamental righs law (MA, very challenging course, with a lot of material to know, but taught in a structured way. Also a very interesting course).
Introduction to Dutch Law (BA, Easyer course)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend doing Introduction to Dutch law in the third period. If not you have to do 3 courses in one of the other periods, which will be quite a challenge.

questions.answer: Food is cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is UM sport where you can try a lot of different things for a monthly subscription. 

There are also student associations.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I liked the Food Bank and Landbouwbelang, but unfortunately I think they will be torn down in a few months. 

De Brandweerkantine is a nice place to hang out, and they have ceap movienights on tuesday. Dr. and dr. Samosa is a nice board game café. 

Maastricht is a nice and safe little city with plenty of things to explore.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are plenty of other cities close by train or bus. The Belgian border is just on the other side of town.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any problems with that.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not anything specific. Just engage in the oppertunities you see.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The cultural differences didn't really stand out to me that much.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The locals speak english quite well, which is very practical.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) The courses are very interesting but challenging. See if you can find easyer courses with only one exam. But if there is a course that really interest you, you should take it regardless of the dificulty. 
2) You can be pretty sure to actually get a place to live if you book a room at UM Geusthouse earlyer in spring. 
3) UM is very helpful with practical stuff.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a swapfiets bike early, as they are popular and rented out pretty quickely.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having friends from other parts of the world and gaining new perspectives.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
